steps.text: Chapter 4.1: Pricing and Financial Performance. Let's read it together, and I'll explain each part as we go.
What does one gram cost?

Product pricing across FMCG categories varies based on ingredient quality, processing techniques, and packaging formats. Comparing products on a price-per-gram basis reveals how premium positioning and raw material costs influence retail strategy.
Assorted Laddoo Box (24 Laddoos)
Assorted Laddoo Box (42 Laddoos)
Ultimate Snack Box (12 Packs)
Assorted Namkeen Combo (4 Packs)
Bars are scaled to the dearest price per gram. Photos: official, eatbetterco.com.
Worked out from the table: 100 ÷ price per gram.
Read the bars, not the box size
The namkeen combo is the cheapest per gram and the laddoo boxes are the dearest. Now look at the two laddoo boxes: is the bigger one cheaper per gram, the way you would expect?
You will check this yourself on a 3D scale in the first activity.
Here's the idea: To compare snack prices fairly, we look at the price for one gram. Divide the price by the grams, and you can compare a small box with a big one.
Three reasons a gram costs what it costs
Raw material Bill of Materials (BOM)
Premium ingredients like dates, almonds, cashews, quinoa, and seeds carry a substantially higher unit cost than refined flour (maida), potatoes, or palm oil used in conventional snacks.
Clean-label value proposition
A value-based pricing premium from health-conscious consumers
Eliminating artificial preservatives, bad fats, and refined sugars commands a value-based pricing premium from health-conscious consumers.
Volume & multi-pack discounting
Shipping and primary packaging overhead is shared across more units.
